question: Across a frozen small set of fusion-defined sarcoma diagnoses, does molecular eligibility retrieval recover source-supported diagnosis-level candidates missed by ordinary disease synonyms and full-text search, with a credible bounded reference set and nontrivial novelty?
priority: Existing rank4 after three independently verified deprioritizations; gate unverified.
selection: Before retrieval, freeze 3-5 diagnoses including EMC, canonical disease synonyms and established defining fusion terms with primary provenance; do not choose based on query success. Enumerate a defensibly bounded complete query corpus with pagination and counts, timestamp/hash raw sources. Separate current records from historical candidates.
validation: Compare condition-only, ordinary synonym/full-text and molecular criteria retrieval. Preserve all comparator IDs, pagination, eligibility source pointers, positive candidates, hard negatives and uncertainty. Source-grounded worker reference labels remain provisional pending coordinator independent verification. No global recall without independent denominator. Diagnosis-level compatibility is not patient eligibility.
novelty: Focused primary prior-art check including TrialGPT and diagnosis/molecular search. Condition-field omission is not unfindability; beating an artificially weak baseline is insufficient.
success: A reproducible useful retrieval gap surviving ordinary synonyms/full-text baselines, credible reference-set construction, plausible generalization and distinct contribution warranting development.
stop: One medium 1800-second fresh-context round, return go/no-go or specific remediable uncertainty. No nested tasks/runners, manuscript rewriting, clinical registry edits, publication/outreach or API/GPU spending. No total daily program pacing cap; bounded rounds remain for coordination.
